title: Verbal Adverbs 8: Mixed Review
description: Synthesis of the verbal adverb track: imperfective and perfective formation, simultaneous vs prior reading, the same-subject rule, register choice, and negation. Today: pull all five threads together and produce the full range.
descriptionRussian: Итоговый урок трека деепричастий: образование на -я / -а и -в / -вшись, одновременное и предшествующее значение, правило общего субъекта, выбор стиля, отрицание. Сегодня: соединяем все пять линий и сами строим формы.
intro: Five checks on any verbal adverb: which aspect the timing calls for, how the form is built, whether the subjects match, whether the register fits, and where the negation goes. The subject check is the one that produces actual errors; the rest produce awkwardness at worst.
rules: The five-step diagnostic: aspect, formation, same subject, register, negation. Run it in order on any gerund.
Imperfective -я / -а expresses simultaneous action; perfective -в / -вшись expresses prior completed action. Both demand the same subject as the main verb.
When subjects differ, rewrite as a когда clause; when subjects match in spoken contexts, the когда clause is also natural; when subjects match in written contexts, the gerund is the natural choice.
Negation with не is regular and goes before the gerund as a separate word. Multiple gerunds can chain inside a single sentence.
A few common verbs (бежать, петь, пить, лить, ждать, мочь) have no imperfective gerund; rewrite them with a когда clause.
examples: Читая книгу, она пила чай. (Imperfective; simultaneous; same subject; written.)
Прочитав книгу, она легла спать. (Perfective; prior; same subject; written.)
Не зная ответа, Маша молчала. (Imperfective; simultaneous; negated; same subject.)
*Открывая дверь, упала ваза → Когда я открывал дверь, упала ваза. (Dangling gerund rewritten with когда clause.)
Войдя в комнату и улыбнувшись, Антон поздоровался. (Perfective gerund chain; prior; same subject.)
Когда я открыл дверь, я вошёл. (Spoken register: когда clause is more natural than the gerund here.)

items.prompt: Recap from L6: in which register is a gerund construction MOST natural?
items.hint: Recall the register call from lesson 6.
items.explanation: Verbal adverbs are at home in the written register: literature, journalism, essays. In conversation, native speakers reach for когда + finite verb even when the gerund is grammatical, so the three spoken options are all wrong.

items.promptEnglish: Reading the book, Masha drank tea.
items.hint: Reading and drinking happen together. Which aspect's gerund expresses simultaneous action?
items.explanation: The simultaneous reading and drinking call for the imperfective gerund Читая. Прочитав ('having read') would imply she finished the book first; читать is the infinitive and читала is the finite past, neither a gerund.

items.promptEnglish: Having finished work, Anton went home.
items.hint: The work is finished BEFORE Anton goes home. Which aspect's gerund expresses prior completion?
items.explanation: Закончив is the perfective gerund: prior completed action. Заканчивая ('while finishing') would describe simultaneous action, a different reading; закончить is the infinitive; закончил is the finite past.

items.promptEnglish: Not knowing the answer, she stayed silent.
items.hint: Negated imperfective gerund. The particle goes directly before the form as a separate word.
items.explanation: Не зная is the negated imperfective gerund, with не standing separate from the form. Не знал is the negated finite past; не знать is the negated infinitive; без + gerund is not a Russian construction.

items.promptEnglish: Which sentence breaks the same-subject rule?
options: Зная город, Маша легко нашла дорогу.
Не понимая инструкций, Иван попросил помощи.
items.hint: Find the option whose two verbs have different subjects.
items.explanation: In 'Подходя к дому, начался дождь,' the implied human approaches but the rain starts: two subjects, so the gerund dangles. The other three sentences each share one subject across both verbs.

items.promptEnglish: Having returned home, Lena called her mom.
items.hint: Reflexive perfective verb; the return happens BEFORE the call. Which form fits?
items.explanation: Вернувшись is the perfective gerund of reflexive вернуться (-ться → -вшись). The return is completed before the call. Возвращаясь is the imperfective gerund (simultaneous); вернуться is the infinitive; вернулась is the finite past.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Imperfective gerund expresses simultaneous action; the subject (мама) is shared.
hints: Watching and cooking happen together. Which form is the imperfective gerund of смотреть?
explanations: Смотря is the imperfective gerund of смотреть (смотрят → смотр- + я → смотря). Mom watches and cooks at the same time. Посмотрев is the perfective gerund (would imply she finished watching first); смотрел is the finite past; смотреть is the infinitive.

errorCorrection.sentence: Молчя в углу, Антон слушал разговор.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Keeping silent in the corner, Anton listened to the conversation.
errorCorrection.explanation: Молчать is imperfective and its third-person plural is молчат, with the stem ending in ч, so the gerund takes -а, not -я: молча. Молчя is the trap of adding -я without that rule, and the spelling -чя does not exist in Russian. Молчав puts a perfective -в suffix on the stem and is not a standard form; Промолчав is the perfective gerund of промолчать ('having stayed silent'), a completed prior action that clashes with the simultaneous listening. Since the silence holds while he listens, the imperfective молча is correct.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Having finished her tea, Lena washed the cup.
errorCorrection.explanation: The gloss 'having finished her tea, then washed the cup' is a sequence: tea finished, then cup washed, which calls for the perfective gerund допив (from допить, drop -ть, add -в). Допивая is the imperfective gerund 'while finishing the tea', which would put the drinking and washing on the same clock and contradicts the prior-completed cue. Допивши is the dated -вши variant; Допивав is not a standard form. Because the drinking completes before the washing, допив is correct.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: When I was walking in the park, it started to rain.
errorCorrection.explanation: A gerund must share its subject with the main verb, but the subject of начался is дождь (the rain), and the rain is not walking in the park, so Гуляя dangles. The fix is a когда clause with its own human subject: Когда я гулял по парку. Погуляв по парку is the perfective gerund ('having walked a while'), which still dangles and changes the timing; Гуляв по парку is not a valid form. English allows 'Walking in the park, it started to rain', but Russian requires the когда rewrite.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Having read the book, she went to bed.
minimalPairs.explanation: Sequential actions: book finished first, sleep after. The perfective Прочитав fits. Читая would mean she goes to bed while still reading, which the sentence does not support.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Not knowing the answer, Masha stayed silent.
minimalPairs.explanation: Both look similar, but the slot expects only the gerund and its negation; the object 'ответа' is already in the sentence after the blank. Adding 'ответа' inside the gerund slot would duplicate it. The clean answer is the bare 'Не зная.'

patternRecognition.question: Which thread of the gerund system does this sentence test?
patternRecognition.explanation: Читая is the imperfective form (-я ending), and the reading runs alongside the drinking. Same-subject rule satisfied (она). This is the canonical simultaneous-action pattern, not prior, dangling, or negated.

patternRecognition.question: Which thread of the gerund system does this sentence test?
patternRecognition.explanation: Прочитав is the perfective form (-в ending). The reading is finished before she goes to sleep. Same-subject rule satisfied (она). This is the canonical prior-action pattern, not simultaneous, dangling, or negated.

patternRecognition.question: Which thread of the gerund system does this sentence test?
patternRecognition.explanation: Two different subjects: the implied human approaches, but the rain starts. The same-subject rule is broken, so this is the dangling pattern. The fix is a когда clause: Когда я подходил к дому, начался дождь.

patternRecognition.sentence: Не понимая инструкций, Иван попросил помощи.
patternRecognition.question: Which thread of the gerund system does this sentence test?
patternRecognition.explanation: Не понимая is a negated imperfective gerund, with не directly before the form. Same-subject rule satisfied (Иван). The state of not understanding holds during the asking, so the operative thread is negation, not a plain aspect or dangling question.

reviewVocab.example: Читая, говоря, видя, зная — несовершенные деепричастия.

reviewVocab.definition: perfective verbal adverb (-в / -вшись; prior completed action)
same-subject rule (the gerund and the main verb must share a subject)
reviewVocab.example: Гуляя по парку, мы говорили — субъект мы для обоих глаголов.

reviewVocab.definition: когда clause (a finite subordinate clause that supplies its own subject; the standard rewrite when the same-subject rule fails)
reviewVocab.example: *Подходя к дому, начался дождь → Когда я подходил к дому, начался дождь.
